title: Genotyping and Phylogenetic Analysis with ViroTrakr Workflows
author: Jayanthi Gangiredla
materials: Reference libraries are available in the history. 3.1.

steps.title: Create or log into account
steps.instruction: Create a GalaxyTrakr account if you are a first‑time user, then log into your GalaxyTrakr account.

steps.title: Upload raw FASTQ files
steps.instruction: Upload raw sequencing data (FASTQ) from your local folder, import reference data, run the ViroTrakr workflow, and retrieve all output files.

substeps.instruction: Click the “Upload” button in the left‑hand menu.
Click “Choose local files”, select the FASTQ files from your local folder, and click “Open”.
Monitor the upload status until it is complete.
Build a list of datasets and then a collection of datasets; the list will appear in the History panel.
Import the reference data files from the Shared Data libraries (they will appear in the History).
Click the “WorkFlows” button in the left‑hand menu, select “Public” workflows, search for “ViroTrakr”, and choose the workflow “Norovirus with reads as input”.
Click the arrowhead button to run the selected workflow.
In each workflow dropdown, select the appropriate input files (uploaded FASTQ files, reference libraries, etc.) and click Run.
Watch the workflow status; each step turns green when finished. The run may take a few minutes or longer depending on data size and system load.

When the run completes, download the output files from the History, which include: Assembly with MEGAHIT, Kraken2 classification report, Report_blasthits_Genotype (best BLAST hits), Genotyping_report (QC statistics and genotyping results), Virus contigs, and Reference_query_phylogenetic_tree (PNG and TXT formats).

steps.title: Download SRA data and run workflow
steps.instruction: Download raw sequencing data from the NCBI SRA using accession numbers, then execute the ViroTrakr workflow as for local FASTQ files.

substeps.instruction: Create a plain‑text file containing one SRA accession number per line; each accession must start with SRR, DRR, or ERR, and save the file locally.
In GalaxyTrakr, click “Upload”, choose “Paste/Fetch data”, select the accession‑list file, click “Choose local file”, then click “Start” to upload the list to your History.
Click the “Tool” button in the left‑hand menu, select “Get Data”, then choose “Faster Download and Extract Reads in FASTQ”.
Set the input type to “List of SRA accession”, select the uploaded list file from the History panel, and click “Run Tool”.
Wait for the FASTQ files to be downloaded from the NCBI SRA database (download time varies with number of files and NCBI server status).
After download, follow the same steps as in “Upload raw FASTQ files” (import reference data, select the “Norovirus with reads as input” workflow, run it, and collect the results).
